I’ve just finished a series of edits: updated AGENTS.md to replace references to mypy with pyaot, added an exemption for tiny changes in the 2B verification rule, and modified the Makefile lint target to run pyaot instead of mypy. I also verified that `make lint` now passes (exit code 0, pyaot reports 0 errors) and that all tests still pass (`make test` shows 123 passed). The next logical step is to record these changes in the project’s journal and commit them to version control, so the history reflects what was done and why.

First, I need to create a comprehensive journal entry. It should include a timestamp, a concise TL;DR, and a detailed description of the changes made, the motivation behind them, and any side effects observed. I should mention the specific bug that was fixed in the SLERP tournament (duplicate and self merges) and the new `merge_key` function, as well as the documentation updates that were required for the audit. I also need to note the switch from mypy to pyaot as the type checker, the updates to AGENTS.md and the Makefile, and the new exemption rule for tiny changes in the 2B verification run. Including the outcomes (tests passing, lint clean) and any remaining open questions will make the entry useful for future reference.

Next, I must stage the modified files (`AGENTS.md`, `Makefile`, and the new `journal.md` entry) with `git add`. Then I’ll create a commit with a clear message that captures the essence of the changes: switching the lint type check from mypy to pyaot and adding the exemption for tiny changes from the 2B runs. Finally, to confirm the commit succeeded and to provide a concise view of recent history, I’ll run `git log --oneline -2`.

All of this can be done in a single Bash command: use a heredoc to append the journal entry to `journal.md`, then `git add` the three files, `git commit` with the appropriate message, and finally `git log --oneline -2` to show the last two commits. This will both document the work and ensure it’s version‑controlled.

Thus, I’ll construct the Bash command accordingly and execute it.

arguments.command:
cat >> /home/lane/MythosMini/journal.md <<'EOF'

## [2026-06-10 20:20] — slerp tournament dedup and AGENTS.md typing/verification rule updates

**TL;DR:** Fixed wasted benchmark evals in the SLERP tournament (self-merges and symmetric duplicate merges now skipped via canonical merge keys); switched the project type checker from mypy to pyaot per user instruction; added a verification-run exemption for tiny non-training changes. 123 tests pass, lint and pyaot clean.

**Long description:** A live 1B-token run (runs/20260610_193911) showed the tournament evaluating merges like gen0_step_00007630+step_00007630@t0.33 — a checkpoint merged with itself — because in build_generation the specialist crosses (wiki/arc/blimp best) can pick the same candidate twice, and slerp of identical states is the identity. The same run also re-evaluated equivalent merges (a+b@t0.50 from the pair sweep plus b+a@t0.50 from the specialist crosses). Fix in src/mythosmini/merging/tournament.py: new merge_key(a, b, t) returning (sorted names, t percent) with t mapped to 1−t when the name order flips (slerp(a,b,t) == slerp(b,a,1−t)); build_generation routes every merge through an add_child closure that skips seen keys, plus an explicit a.name == b.name guard on specialist crosses. Proving tests added to tests/test_merging.py (merge_key canonicalization, no self-merge names, no duplicate canonical keys across a generation). The docs audit in make lint caught the missing merge_key entry; added it and updated build_generation in docs/functions.md. Started the mandatory 2B verification run, then the user amended the rules: tiny changes that do not affect training behavior are exempt, so the run was killed during token caching (no scores.md row; partial run dir left under runs/). Per the same user instruction, AGENTS.md now says ignore mypy and use pyaot.py as the type checker (fix pyaot bugs when found, follow its advice), and the Makefile lint target swaps `mypy --strict` for `pyaot.py .`.

**What worked:** make test 123 passed. make lint exit 0 with the new pyaot step ("pyaot: checked 61 file(s) — 0 error(s)"). The same run's log confirmed the live duplicate evals the fix targets: identical-weight merges re-scored with arc varying 30.6–31.2, exposing ~±0.4 benchmark noise on ARC.

**What failed:** First docs audit run: "error: missing documentation in docs/functions.md for: src/mythosmini/merging/tournament.py: function 'merge_key'" — fixed by adding the entry. My initial dedup test had dead variables that violated the no-dead-code rule; rewritten before commit. Earlier inline sanity script asserted 7 children where 9 was correct (b+a@t0.33 reverses to a+b@t0.67, distinct from the sweep's t0.65 — not a duplicate).

**What was kept / discarded:** Kept merge_key, the add_child dedup, the three new tests, the AGENTS.md and Makefile changes. Discarded the in-flight 2B verification run (killed at ~3% token caching) under the new exemption rule.

**Open questions / next steps:** Benchmark noise (~±0.4 ARC on identical weights) means champion selection can chase lucky evals; averaging repeat evals for top candidates is a backlog candidate. Checkpoint cadence gives only 4 seeds per run; denser late-training checkpoints would give the tournament more diversity. mypy and types-tqdm remain pinned in requirements.txt though lint no longer runs mypy — removing them is its own dependency task.
EOF
git add AGENTS.md Makefile journal.md && git commit -m "switch lint type check from mypy to pyaot and exempt tiny changes from 2b runs" && git log --oneline -2
